questions.stem: Which of these quantities is a vector?
options: A velocity of 20 km/h due north
questions.explanation: A vector has both magnitude and direction, and a velocity due north has both. Speed, mass and distance have magnitude only, so they are scalars.

questions.stem: A person walks 3 km east and then 3 km west. Their distance travelled and the magnitude of their displacement are:
questions.explanation: Distance is a scalar that adds every leg, 6 km. Displacement is the vector from start to finish, and the person is back where they started, so it is 0.

questions.stem: Two arrows drawn in different places on a page represent equal vectors when they have:
options: the same starting point and the same end point only
the same direction, of any magnitude
the same magnitude and the same direction
the same magnitude, in any direction
questions.explanation: Vectors are equal when magnitude and direction both match, wherever they are drawn. Requiring the same starting point is too strict, since equal vectors can be parallel translations of each other.

questions.stem: Compared with a non-zero vector a, the vector −2a has:
options: twice the magnitude and the opposite direction
twice the magnitude and the same direction
half the magnitude and the opposite direction
the same magnitude and the opposite direction
questions.explanation: Multiplying by a negative scalar reverses the direction, and the size of the scalar, 2, doubles the magnitude. A scalar of −1 alone would keep the magnitude the same.

questions.stem: The length (magnitude) of the displacement vector 3i − 4j is:
questions.explanation: |3i − 4j| = √(3² + (−4)²) = √25 = 5. Adding the components gives −1 or 7, and 25 forgets the square root.

questions.stem: The position vector of the point (3, −2) can be written as:
questions.explanation: The x-coordinate multiplies i and the y-coordinate multiplies j, so (3, −2) has position vector 3i − 2j, the column vector with entries 3 and −2. Swapping the components gives −2i + 3j.

questions.stem: The unit vector in the direction of 5i + 12j is:
questions.explanation: Divide the vector by its magnitude √(25 + 144) = 13. Dividing by 17 adds the components, and dividing by 169 uses the square of the magnitude.

questions.stem: The angle that −3i + 3j makes with the positive x-axis, measured anticlockwise, is:
questions.explanation: tan θ = 3/(−3) = −1, and the vector points into the second quadrant (x negative, y positive), so θ = 135°. A calculator gives −45°, which is the fourth-quadrant angle with the same tangent.

questions.stem: In polar form (r, θ), with θ measured anticlockwise from the positive x-axis, the vector i + √3 j is:
questions.explanation: r = √(1 + 3) = 2 and tan θ = √3, so θ = 60° in the first quadrant. The angle 30° comes from inverting the tangent ratio, x over y.

questions.stem: The vector with polar form (10, 210°) in Cartesian form is:
questions.explanation: x = 10 cos 210° = −5√3 and y = 10 sin 210° = −5, placing the vector in the third quadrant. Swapping sine and cosine gives −5i − 5√3 j.

questions.stem: In polar form (r, θ), with 0° ≤ θ < 360°, the vector −4i − 4j is:
questions.explanation: r = √(16 + 16) = 4√2 and the vector is in the third quadrant at 45° past the negative x-axis, so θ = 225°. The calculator angle tan⁻¹(1) = 45° ignores the quadrant.

questions.stem: By the triangle rule, for points A, B and C the vector AB + BC equals:
questions.explanation: Travelling from A to B and then B to C has the same overall effect as travelling from A to C. CA is the same length but in the opposite direction.

questions.stem: In parallelogram OABC, OA = a and OC = c. The vector AC equals:
questions.explanation: AC = AO + OC = −a + c = c − a. The vector a + c is the other diagonal, OB.

questions.stem: Points A and B have position vectors a and b. The position vector of the midpoint M of AB is:
questions.explanation: OM = OA + (1/2)AB = a + (1/2)(b − a) = (a + b)/2. The vector (b − a)/2 is AM, from A to the midpoint, not from the origin.

questions.stem: If a = 2i + j and b = −i + 3j, then 2a − b is:
questions.explanation: 2a = 4i + 2j, and subtracting b gives (4 + 1)i + (2 − 3)j = 5i − j. Adding b instead gives 3i + 5j.

questions.stem: For the points A(1, 4) and B(5, 1), the vector AB and its magnitude are:
questions.explanation: AB = b − a = (5 − 1)i + (1 − 4)j = 4i − 3j, with magnitude √(16 + 9) = 5. The vector −4i + 3j is BA, the reverse direction.

questions.stem: The midpoint of the segment joining A(−2, 3) and B(6, −1) is:
questions.explanation: Average the coordinates: ((−2 + 6)/2, (3 − 1)/2) = (2, 1). Halving the differences instead gives (4, −2), which is half of AB.

questions.stem: The point P divides the segment AB internally in the ratio 1 : 3, where A is (2, 5) and B is (10, 1). The coordinates of P are:
questions.explanation: P is one quarter of the way from A to B: OP = a + (1/4)(b − a) = (2, 5) + (1/4)(8, −4) = (4, 4). Going three quarters of the way gives (8, 2), the 3 : 1 point.

questions.stem: For vectors a = a₁i + a₂j and b = b₁i + b₂j at angle θ, the scalar product a · b equals:
options: |a||b| sin θ, which also equals a₁b₁ + a₂b₂
|a||b| cos θ, which also equals a₁b₂ + a₂b₁
|a||b| cos θ, which also equals a₁b₁ + a₂b₂
questions.explanation: The geometric and component forms of the dot product agree: |a||b| cos θ = a₁b₁ + a₂b₂. The result is a scalar, not a vector.

questions.stem: The scalar product (2i + 3j) · (4i − j) is:
questions.explanation: Multiply matching components and add: 2 × 4 + 3 × (−1) = 8 − 3 = 5. The answer is a number, so 8i − 3j is not a scalar product.

questions.stem: Vectors a and b have |a| = 4, |b| = 5 and an angle of 60° between them. The value of a · b is:
questions.explanation: a · b = 4 × 5 × cos 60° = 20 × 0.5 = 10. Using sin 60° gives 17.3, and leaving out the cosine gives 20.

questions.stem: For any vector a, the scalar product a · a equals:
questions.explanation: The angle between a and itself is 0°, so a · a = |a||a| cos 0° = |a|². This is often used to find a magnitude.

questions.stem: The angle between 3i + 4j and 5i + 12j, to one decimal place, is:
questions.explanation: cos θ = (15 + 48)/(5 × 13) = 63/65, so θ = 14.3°. The angle 53.1° is the direction of 3i + 4j alone, measured from the x-axis.

questions.stem: Two non-zero vectors have a scalar product of 0. The vectors are:
options: parallel and in the same direction
questions.explanation: a · b = |a||b| cos θ = 0 with non-zero vectors forces cos θ = 0, so θ = 90°. Parallel vectors give the largest possible size of a · b, not 0.

questions.stem: The vectors ki + 2j and 3i − 6j are perpendicular when k equals:
questions.explanation: Perpendicular vectors have scalar product 0: 3k − 12 = 0, so k = 4. Making them parallel instead would need k = −1.

questions.stem: The vectors 2i − 3j and mi + 9j are parallel when m equals:
questions.explanation: Parallel vectors are scalar multiples: 9 = −3 × (−3), so mi + 9j = −3(2i − 3j) and m = −6. The perpendicular condition 2m − 27 = 0 gives 13.5.

questions.stem: The scalar projection of a = 4i + 3j onto b = 3i + 4j is:
questions.explanation: The scalar projection is a · b̂ = (12 + 12)/|b| = 24/5 = 4.8. The value 24 is a · b without dividing by |b|.

questions.stem: The vector projection of a = 2i + 3j onto b = 4i − 2j is:
questions.explanation: (a · b / b · b)b = (2/20)(4i − 2j) = 0.4i − 0.2j. The vector 0.8i − 0.4j is twice as long, as if b · b were 10 rather than 4² + 2² = 20.

questions.stem: For a = 2i + 3j and b = 4i − 2j, the component of a perpendicular to b is:
questions.explanation: Subtract the vector projection from a: (2i + 3j) − (0.4i − 0.2j) = 1.6i + 3.2j. Check: (1.6i + 3.2j) · (4i − 2j) = 6.4 − 6.4 = 0.

questions.stem: A force of 20 N acts at 30° above the positive x-axis. In component form it is:
questions.explanation: The horizontal component is 20 cos 30° = 10√3 and the vertical component is 20 sin 30° = 10. Swapping sine and cosine gives 10i + 10√3 j.

questions.stem: Forces 3i + 2j, −5i + j and 4i − 6j newtons act on a particle. The magnitude of the resultant force is:
questions.explanation: The resultant is (3 − 5 + 4)i + (2 + 1 − 6)j = 2i − 3j, with magnitude √(4 + 9) = √13. The value 13 forgets the square root.

questions.stem: A particle is in equilibrium under forces F₁ = 3i − 2j, F₂ = −i + 5j and a third force F₃ (in newtons). F₃ is:
questions.explanation: In equilibrium the forces sum to zero, so F₃ = −(F₁ + F₂) = −(2i + 3j) = −2i − 3j. The vector 2i + 3j is the sum of the other two, not the balancing force.

questions.stem: A 5 kg block is held at rest on a smooth plane inclined at 30° by a force parallel to the plane. Taking g = 9.8 m/s², the size of that force is:
questions.explanation: Along the plane, the force balances the component of weight down the slope: mg sin θ = 5 × 9.8 × 0.5 = 24.5 N. The value 42.4 N is mg cos θ, the component into the plane.

questions.stem: For the same 5 kg block held on the smooth 30° plane by a force parallel to the plane, the normal reaction force, with g = 9.8 m/s², is:
questions.explanation: Perpendicular to the plane, the normal reaction balances the weight component mg cos θ = 49 × cos 30° = 42.4 N, because the holding force is parallel to the plane. It is less than the full weight of 49 N.

questions.stem: A 5 kg block is held at rest on a smooth plane inclined at 30° by a horizontal force. Taking g = 9.8 m/s², the size of the horizontal force is:
questions.explanation: Resolving along the plane, F cos 30° = mg sin 30°, so F = mg tan 30° = 49 × 0.577 = 28.3 N. The value 24.5 N is the answer for a force parallel to the plane.

questions.stem: Speed is related to velocity as:
options: the component of velocity along the x-axis
the magnitude of the velocity vector
the direction of the velocity vector
the velocity vector multiplied by time
questions.explanation: Velocity is a vector, and speed is its magnitude, which has no direction. The x-component is only part of the velocity.

questions.stem: A plane heads due north at 300 km/h in still air, and a wind blows from the west at 40 km/h. The plane's resultant speed and true bearing are:
questions.explanation: The velocities are perpendicular, so the speed is √(300² + 40²) = 302.7 km/h; a wind from the west pushes the plane east, so the bearing is tan⁻¹(40/300) = 7.6° east of north. A bearing of 352.4°T would mean drifting west.

questions.stem: A boat crosses a river 60 m wide, steering straight across at 4 m/s relative to the water, while the current flows at 3 m/s. The time to cross and the distance carried downstream are:
questions.explanation: Only the 4 m/s across the river affects crossing time: 60 ÷ 4 = 15 s. In that time the current carries the boat 3 × 15 = 45 m downstream. Using the resultant 5 m/s gives 12 s, which is wrong because the current does not help the crossing.

questions.stem: A yacht has velocity 3i + 4j m/s and a ferry has velocity −i + 2j m/s. The velocity of the yacht relative to the ferry is:
questions.explanation: The velocity of the yacht relative to the ferry is the yacht's velocity minus the ferry's: (3 + 1)i + (4 − 2)j = 4i + 2j. The vector −4i − 2j is the velocity of the ferry relative to the yacht.

questions.stem: Car P travels east at 60 km/h and car Q travels north at 80 km/h. The speed of Q relative to P is:
questions.explanation: Q's velocity minus P's is −60i + 80j, with magnitude √(3600 + 6400) = 100 km/h. Subtracting the speeds, 80 − 60 = 20, ignores that the cars move at right angles.
